title: The Flannan Isles Mystery
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the 1900 disappearance of three lighthouse keepers from the Flannan Isles lighthouse on Eilean Mòr (Island More) in the Outer Hebrides, Scotland. They cover the remote setting, how Scottish lighthouse keeping worked under the Northern Lighthouse Board, the steamship Archer noticing the light was out, the relief ship Hesperus and Joseph Moore's discovery of an apparently undisturbed station with two sets of oilskins missing, the storm damage evidence, and the fabricated log book and Wilfred Wilson Gibson poem that embellished the story. They weigh explanations including storm wind, a fight involving Donald MacArthur, and supernatural theories (Kelpie, pagan sacrifice), favoring a rogue wave theory, and mention Mike Dash's research debunking the embellishments and Robert Muirhead's investigation. The episode closes with a listener mail about dingoes and why domestic dogs bark.

segments.title: Opening banter and The Lighthouse movie
segments.summary: Hosts pre-apologize for Scottish name pronunciations and discuss how The Lighthouse film connects to the Flannan Isles mystery.

segments.title: Setting: Island More and the Flannan Isles
segments.summary: Describes the Eilean Mòr lighthouse, its 200-foot cliff, the windy and treacherous waters of the Outer Hebrides, and the island's remoteness and folklore.

segments.title: Lighthouse keeper life and the Northern Lighthouse Board
segments.summary: Explains the Northern Lighthouse Board, staffing hierarchy of principal keeper, assistants and occasional keepers, rotation, and the low rate of keepers found asleep on duty.

segments.title: The three keepers and the Archer sighting
segments.summary: Introduces the keepers James Ducat, Thomas Marshall, Donald MacArthur and William Ross, and the steamship Archer passing by in December 1900 noticing the light was out.

segments.title: Relief ship Hesperus and the discovery
segments.summary: The relief ship Hesperus arrives after Christmas with no one greeting it; Joseph Moore goes ashore and finds the station apparently abandoned, with two sets of oilskins missing.

segments.title: State of the station and embellished accounts
segments.summary: Details the undisturbed keeper's house, and how a fabricated log book and Wilfred Wilson Gibson's poem added creepy embellishments later debunked by Mike Dash.

segments.title: Physical evidence of storm damage
segments.summary: Describes storm evidence: the crane intact, a smashed crate and buoy high on the cliff, twisted railings, a 2,000-pound stone, torn-up tracks and turf.

segments.title: Theories: wind, fight, and supernatural explanations
segments.summary: Robert Muirhead's report considers wind blowing men off the island but favors a wave; theories of a fight involving MacArthur and supernatural explanations such as the Kelpie and pagan sacrifice are dismissed.

segments.title: Rogue wave theory and later investigations
segments.summary: Hosts favor a rogue wave explanation involving two successive waves, timing of the event before sunset on December 15, and Robert Alderbert's 1950s experiments and observations.

segments.title: Listener mail: dingoes and dog barking
segments.summary: A listener follow-up on the dingo episode explains that wild adult dogs rarely bark while domestic dogs do, linked to domestication and suspended adolescence; the hosts thank Peter Bonnier.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and invite listener mail.
